players.product: CMP pads, cleans & slurries and lithography ancillary materials for leading-edge logic/memory (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 (a record quarter; eighth consecutive quarter of organic growth): net sales $1.3 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 11% sequentially (organic +17%, double-digit growth in both segments); adjusted operating EBITDA $411 million, up 22%, margin 31.3% (up more than 125 basis points); adjusted EPS $1.08, up 33%. By geography, Taiwan was up 25% year-over-year on a top line basis and Korea up 17%.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $1.3 billion (+18% YoY, +11% QoQ); adj. EBITDA $411 million (31.3%); adj. EPS $1.08; Taiwan up 25%, Korea up 17%

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor Technologies net sales $722 million with 12% organic growth year-over-year, led by advanced logic and HBM chips, with particularly strong gains in CMP consumables; the quarter included $20 million of inventory restocking, particularly in mature nodes, after customers managed inventory carefully in Q4. Segment adjusted operating EBITDA margin 36.4%, up 130 basis points from Q4. Q2 outlook: Semi sequential net sales roughly flat with margins in the mid-thirties.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Technologies $722 million (+12% organic); $20 million restocking; EBITDA margin 36.4%; Q2 roughly flat

quarterly_data.signal: Node roadmap: 3 nanometer volumes continue to scale, meaningful activity starting at 2 nanometer (2 nm starting in the second half), and Angstrom-era nodes (16, 14, 10) are the main focus of R&D engagement with customers. Higher node complexity means more CMP process steps, more advanced cleans and more intricate lithography patterning. New CMP pads and advanced cleans launched for 2 nanometer and Angstrom-era nodes; POR wins in lithography in both ArF and EUV sublayers; positive customer progress on HBM4 (timing left to customers). 2025 was a record year with POR wins in every line of business.

Fab utilization: mainstream logic went from the mid-70s last year to the high 70s and into the low 80s in Q1, with further sequential improvement expected; DRAM finished 2025 in the mid-80s, trending into the high 80s and possibly above 90% in the second half; NAND moved from mid-70s to high 70s and possibly into the low 80s in the second half. Management said wafer capacity remains tight and customers are allocating it to the highest value applications; memory pricing is not having a material impact because exposure is to premium devices and AI-led infrastructure growth offsets consumer softness. China semiconductor exposure is mostly mature logic, not advanced memory.
quarterly_data.figure: DRAM high 80s, maybe even reaching above 90% in 2H; mainstream logic low 80s in Q1; NAND low 80s in 2H

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: opened a 385,000 square foot facility in Delaware in March, with its first line already operational and in customer qualification; a new Taiwan site (production, clean rooms, warehousing, R&D labs) will finish equipment installation this year and be fully operational in early 2027. Both mainly expand CMP materials capacity. Q1 capex included about one-third of the $61.5 million Taiwan facility investment; 2026 capex expected at approximately 9% of sales, falling to about 6% of net sales longer term. Capacity has been added in every semiconductor product line, and management says capacity is sufficient to scale Angstrom-era nodes.
quarterly_data.figure: 385,000 square foot Delaware facility; $61.5 million Taiwan investment; capex approximately 9% of sales (2026), 6% of net sales long term

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance raised: net sales $5.225 billion-$5.375 billion (5% increase at the midpoint), adjusted operating EBITDA $1.535 billion-$1.625 billion, adjusted EPS $3.80-$4.14, adjusted free cash flow $500 million-$600 million. MSI wafer start growth assumption raised to mid-single digits to high single digits (from mid-single digits). Q2 net sales expected up mid-single digits sequentially. Guidance assumes about $20 million of geopolitical inflation headwinds (raw materials, logistics) for the rest of 2026, mostly offset by pricing actions; no near-term operational disruptions expected.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $5.225 billion-$5.375 billion; adj. EBITDA $1.535 billion-$1.625 billion; adj. EPS $3.80-$4.14; ~$20 million inflation headwind

players.product: CMP pads & slurries, photoresists, advanced-packaging laminates (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect Solutions (ICS) net sales $593 million with 22% organic growth, led by advanced packaging and interconnects and thermal management; those core areas (advanced packaging, thermal management, AI PCBs) grew more than 50% year-over-year on data center demand and ramps of shorter-cycle POR wins from last year. ICS adjusted operating EBITDA margin 28.5%, up 280 basis points sequentially. Q2 outlook: ICS sequential net sales growth in the high single digits with margins in the mid to high twenties.
quarterly_data.figure: ICS $593 million (+22% organic); core AI areas more than 50% YoY; EBITDA margin 28.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging is expected to be a core growth driver for years as the industry moves from shrink to stack: larger package sizes and higher layer counts mean more Qnity content per device. In advanced interconnects Qnity is winning new business with AI PCB fabs for the leading hyperscalers and premium smartphone OEMs; AI PCBs need finer lines and spaces and more layers, which suits its metallization business (R&D was refocused on this market in the 2023 downturn). New wins in AI PCB fine-line interconnect, copper and solder products.

Thermal management: the portfolio removes heat across the whole system, with progress in thermal pads, liquid gap fillers and phase change materials; management expects advanced packaging and thermal to stay the fastest-growing parts of the portfolio. ICS capacity capex is small, modular and quick to scale, and Qnity is investing in line with customers' advanced packaging capacity additions.

Announced a new collaboration with NVIDIA on materials R&D for next gen AI, high-performance computing and advanced packaging, combining Qnity's materials expertise with NVIDIA's modeling and simulation; Qnity was also included in Apple's American Manufacturing Program. Management said OEMs are now getting involved in material selection and design because of signal reliability, power efficiency and thermal management demands.

Management said data centers are approaching probably 20% of the portfolio (to be confirmed at year end). The PCB area metric used as the ICS benchmark grew in the low double-digit range last year and is expected in the mid-single-digit to high single-digit range this year, similar to MSI; ICS outperformance comes from the three growth areas.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers approaching 20% of the portfolio; PCB area metric mid-single-digit to high single-digit (2026)
